newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rates fall in liquid market.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rates fall in liquid market.

text.p: MANILA, Jan 3 (Friday) - Philippine interbank call loan rates fell on Friday to an average of 11.21875 percent from 12.8125 percent after the maturing of 4.5 billion pesos worth of T-bills led to ample liquidity, dealers said.

The easing in rates does not yet take into account the impact of the one percentage-point cut in reserve requirements since banks were only covering reserve positions for Thursday. The cut took effect on Friday.

The market also experienced increased liquidity since money that used to go to reverse repos was not reinvested after the government decided to impose a 20 percent final tax on these instruments starting January 2.
"It's pretty much liquid," a trader from a big bank said.
The market had 24 lenders and 16 borrowers. Due to the low demand for funds, market volume thinned to 7.665 billion pesos from 28.327 billion pesos.
Looking ahead, the cut in reserve requirement could soften the pressure for interest rates to rise on Monday due to the weekend covering, a trader said.
At the secondary market trading of T-bills, banks were snapping up short-term T-bills after they decided not to invest in reverse repos.
Traders said the 20 percent tax effectively lowered the yield on reverse repos versus T-bills.

According to a Reuter poll of six institutions, banks were quoting bid rates of 11.375 to 11.70 percent on three-month bills; 11.65 to 12.0 percent on six months; and 12.10 to 12.50 on the one-year bills.
